entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.1">Lev 15:1</reference> <div eID="gen1344" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1345" type="x-p"/> The Uncleanness of Secretions. - These include (1) a running issue from a man (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.2-Lev.15.2">Lev 15:2-15); (2</reference>) involuntary emission of seed (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.16">Lev 15:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.15.17">Lev 15:17</reference>), and the emission of seed in sexual intercourse (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.18">Lev 15:18</reference>); (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.3">3</reference>) the monthly period of a woman (Lev 15:19-24); (4) a diseased issue of blood from a woman (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.25-Lev.15.30">Lev 15:25-30</reference>). They consist, therefore, of two diseased and two natural secretions from the organs of generation.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.2-Lev.15.3">Lev 15:2-3</reference> <div eID="gen1345" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1346" type="x-p"/> The <hi type="italic">running issue from a man</hi> is not described with sufficient clearness for us to be able to determine with certainty what disease is referred to: “if a man becomes flowing out of his flesh, he is unclean in his flux.” That even here the term flesh is not a euphemism for the organ of generation, as is frequently assumed, is evident from <reference osisRef="Lev.15.13">Lev 15:13</reference>, “he shall wash his clothes and bathe his <hi type="italic">flesh</hi> in water,” when compared with <reference osisRef="Lev.16.23-Lev.16.24">Lev 16:23-24</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.16.28">Lev 16:28</reference>, etc., where flesh cannot possibly have any such meaning. The “flesh” is the body as in <reference osisRef="Lev.15.7">Lev 15:7</reference>, “whoever touches the flesh of him that hath the issue,” as compared with <reference osisRef="Lev.15.19">Lev 15:19</reference>, “whosoever toucheth her.” At the same time, the agreement between the law relating to the man with an issue and that concerning the woman with an issue (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.19">Lev 15:19</reference>, “her issue in her flesh”) points unmistakeably to a secretion from the sexual organs. Only the seat of the disease is not more closely defined. The issue of the man is not a hemorrhoidal disease, for nothing is said about a flow of blood; still less is it a syphilitic suppuration (<hi type="italic">gonorrhaea virulenta</hi>), for the occurrence of this at all in antiquity is very questionable; but it is either a diseased flow of <hi type="italic">semen</hi> (<hi type="italic">gonorrhaea</hi>), i.e., an involuntary flow drop by drop arising from weakness of the organ, as <hi type="italic">Jerome</hi> and the Rabbins assume, or more probably, simply <hi type="italic">blenorrhaea urethrae</hi>, a discharge of mucus arising from a catarrhal affection of the mucous membrane of the urethra (<hi type="italic">urethritis</hi>). The participle זב יהיה is expressive of continued duration. In <reference osisRef="Lev.15.3">Lev 15:3</reference> the uncleanness is still more closely defined: “whether his flesh run with his issue, or his flesh closes before his issue,” i.e., whether the member lets the matter flow out or by closing retains it, “it is his uncleanness,” i.e., in the latter case as well as the former it is uncleanness to him, he is unclean. For the “closing” is only a temporary obstruction, brought about by some particular circumstance.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.18">Lev 15:18</reference> <hi type="italic">Sexual connection</hi>. “If a man lie with a woman with the emission of seed, both shall be unclean till the evening, and bathe themselves in water.” Consequently it was not the <hi type="italic">concubitus</hi> as such which defiled, as many erroneously suppose, but the emission of seed in the <hi type="italic">coitus</hi>. This explains the law and custom, of abstaining from conjugal intercourse during the preparation for acts of divine worship, or the performance of the same (<reference osisRef="Exod.19.5">Exo 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.21.5-1Sam.21.6">1Sa 21:5-6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Sam.11.4">2Sa 11:4</reference>), in which many other nations resembled the Israelites. (For proofs see Leyrer’s article in Herzog’s Cyclopaedia, and <hi type="italic">Knobel</hi> <hi type="italic">in loco</hi>, though the latter is wrong in supposing that conjugal intercourse itself defiled.)

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.19-Lev.15.23">Lev 15:19-23</reference> <hi type="italic">The menses of a woman</hi>. - “If a woman have an issue, (if) blood is her issue in her flesh, she shall be seven days in her uncleanness.” As the discharge does not last as a rule more than four or five days, the period of seven days was fixed on account of the significance of the number seven. In this condition she rendered every one who touched her unclean (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.19">Lev 15:19</reference>), everything upon which she lay or sat (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.20">Lev 15:20</reference>), every one who touched her bed or whatever she sat upon (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.21">Lev 15:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.15.22">Lev 15:22</reference>), also any one who touched the blood upon her bed or seat (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.23">Lev 15:23</reference>, where הוּא and בּו are to be referred to דּם); and they remained unclean till the evening, when they had to wash their clothes and bathe themselves.
entries.content_plain: Lev 15:19-23 The menses of a woman. - “If a woman have an issue, (if) blood is her issue in her flesh, she shall be seven days in her uncleanness.” As the discharge does not last as a rule more than four or five days, the period of seven days was fixed on account of the significance of the number seven. In this condition she rendered every one who touched her unclean (Lev 15:19), everything upon which she lay or sat (Lev 15:20), every one who touched her bed or whatever she sat upon (Lev 15:21, Lev 15:22), also any one who touched the blood upon her bed or seat (Lev 15:23, where הוּא and בּו are to be referred to דּם); and they remained unclean till the evening, when they had to wash their clothes and bathe themselves.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.24">Lev 15:24</reference> <div eID="gen1351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1352" type="x-p"/> If a man lay with her and her uncleanness came upon him, he became unclean for seven days, and the bed upon which he lay became unclean as well. The meaning cannot be merely if he lie upon the same bed with her, but if he have conjugal intercourse, as is evident from <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">Lev 20:18</reference> and Num 5:13 (cf. <reference osisRef="Gen.26.10">Gen 26:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.34.2">Gen 34:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gen.35.22">Gen 35:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.2.22">1Sa 2:22</reference>). It cannot be adduced as an objection to this explanation, which is the only admissible one, that according to <reference osisRef="Lev.18.19">Lev 18:19</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">Lev 20:18</reference> intercourse with a woman during her menses was an accursed crime, to be punished by extermination. For the law in <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">Lev 20:18</reference> refers partly to conjugal intercourse during the hemorrhage of a woman after child-birth, as the similarity of the words in <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">Lev 20:18</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.12.7">Lev 12:7</reference> (דּמיה מקור) clearly proves, and to the case of a man attempting cohabitation with a woman during her menstruation. The verse before us, on the contrary, refers simply to the possibility of menstruation commencing during the act of conjugal intercourse, when the man would be involuntarily defiled through the unexpected uncleanness of the woman.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.25-Lev.15.27">Lev 15:25-27</reference> <hi type="italic">Diseased issue from a woman</hi>. - If an issue of blood in a woman flowed many days away from (not in) the time of her monthly uncleanness, or if it flowed beyond her monthly uncleanness, she was to be unclean as long as her unclean issue continued, just as in the days of her monthly uncleanness, and she defiled her couch as well as everything upon which she sat, as in the other case, also every one who touched either her or these things.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.28-Lev.15.31">Lev 15:28-31</reference> <div eID="gen1352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1353" type="x-p"/> After the issue had ceased, she was to purify herself like the man with an issue, as described in <reference osisRef="Lev.15.13">Lev 15:13</reference>-15. - Obedience to these commands is urged in <reference osisRef="Lev.15.31">Lev 15:31</reference> : “Cause that the children of Israel free themselves from their uncleanness, that they die not through their uncleanness, by defiling My dwelling in the midst of them.” הזּיר, <hi type="italic">Hiphil</hi>, to cause that a person keeps aloof from anything, or loosens himself from it, from נזר, <hi type="italic">Niphal</hi> to separate one’s self, signifies here deliverance from the state of uncleanness, purification from it. Continuance in it was followed by death, not merely in the particular instance in which an unclean man ventured to enter the sanctuary, but as a general fact, because uncleanness as irreconcilable with the calling of Israel to be a holy nation, in the midst of which Jehovah the Holy One had His dwelling-place (<reference osisRef="Lev.11.44">Lev 11:44</reference>), and continuance in uncleanness without the prescribed purification was a disregard of the holiness of Jehovah, and involved rebellion against Him and His ordinances of grace.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.15.32-Lev.15.33">Lev 15:32-33</reference> <hi type="italic">Concluding formula</hi>. The words, “<hi type="italic">him that lieth with her that is unclean,</hi>” are more general than the expression, “lie with her,” in <reference osisRef="Lev.15.24">Lev 15:24</reference>, and involve not only intercourse with an unclean woman, but lying by her side upon one and the same bed. The Day of Atonement - Leviticus 16 <div eID="gen1353" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1354" type="x-p"/> The sacrifices and purifications enjoined thus far did not suffice to complete the reconciliation between the congregation of Israel, which was called to be a holy nation, but in its very nature was still altogether involved in sin and uncleanness, and Jehovah the Holy One-that is to say, to restore the perfect reconciliation and true vital fellowship of the nation with its God, in accordance with the idea and object of the old covenant - because, even with the most scrupulous observance of these directions, many sins and defilements would still remain unacknowledged, and therefore without expiation, and would necessarily produce in the congregation a feeling of separation from its God, so that it would be unable to attain to the true joyousness of access to the throne of grace, and to the place of reconciliation with God. This want was met by the appointment of a yearly general and perfect expiation of all the sins and uncleanness which had remained unatoned for and uncleansed in the course of the year. In this respect the laws of sacrifice and purification received their completion and finish in the institution of the festival of atonement, which provided for the congregation of Israel the highest and most comprehensive expiation that was possible under the Old Testament. Hence the law concerning the day of atonement formed a fitting close to the ordinances designed to place the Israelites in fellowship with their God, and raise the promise of Jehovah, “I will be your God,” into a living truth. This law is described in the present chapter, and contains (1) the instructions as to the performance of the general expiation for the year (vv. 2-28), and (2) directions for the celebration of this festival every year (<reference osisRef="Lev.16.29-Lev.16.34">Lev 16:29-34</reference>). From the expiation effected upon this day it received the name of “<hi type="italic">day of expiations,</hi>” i.e., of the highest expiation (<reference osisRef="Lev.23.27">Lev 23:27</reference>). The Rabbins call it briefly יומא, the day κατ ̓ ἐξοχήν.  <chapter eID="Lev.15"/> <div eID="gen1354" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
Lev 15:32-33 Concluding formula. The words, “him that lieth with her that is unclean,” are more general than the expression, “lie with her,” in Lev 15:24, and involve not only intercourse with an unclean woman, but lying by her side upon one and the same bed. The Day of Atonement - Leviticus 16 
 
 The sacrifices and purifications enjoined thus far did not suffice to complete the reconciliation between the congregation of Israel, which was called to be a holy nation, but in its very nature was still altogether involved in sin and uncleanness, and Jehovah the Holy One-that is to say, to restore the perfect reconciliation and true vital fellowship of the nation with its God, in accordance with the idea and object of the old covenant - because, even with the most scrupulous observance of these directions, many sins and defilements would still remain unacknowledged, and therefore without expiation, and would necessarily produce in the congregation a feeling of separation from its God, so that it would be unable to attain to the true joyousness of access to the throne of grace, and to the place of reconciliation with God. This want was met by the appointment of a yearly general and perfect expiation of all the sins and uncleanness which had remained unatoned for and uncleansed in the course of the year. In this respect the laws of sacrifice and purification received their completion and finish in the institution of the festival of atonement, which provided for the congregation of Israel the highest and most comprehensive expiation that was possible under the Old Testament. Hence the law concerning the day of atonement formed a fitting close to the ordinances designed to place the Israelites in fellowship with their God, and raise the promise of Jehovah, “I will be your God,” into a living truth. This law is described in the present chapter, and contains (1) the instructions as to the performance of the general expiation for the year (vv. 2-28), and (2) directions for the celebration of this festival every year (Lev 16:29-34). From the expiation effected upon this day it received the name of “day of expiations,” i.e., of the highest expiation (Lev 23:27). The Rabbins call it briefly יומא, the day κατ ̓ ἐξοχήν.
